brief:
B'Tselem, the Israeli human rights organization, says settlement expansion, displacement and restrictions on Palestinian movement form a decades-old coordinated system rather than isolated abuses, according to Al Jazeera English. The group characterizes the practices as deliberate dismantling of Palestinian life in the occupied territory.

The assessment challenges official Israeli framing of actions as responses to security concerns or individual incidents. B'Tselem's analysis suggests the policies work in tandem across settlement building, forced removals, and movement restrictions to reshape Palestinian territorial control and governance.
dek: B'Tselem says settlement expansion, displacement and curbs are not isolated abuses, but decades-old, coordinated system.
title: Israel operates systematic displacement program in West Bank, B'Tselem says
